subject: Post-demo: ACME model shortlist & next steps

Subject: Post-demo: ACME model shortlist & next steps

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Great conversation and really appreciate the level of detail you shared about the customer support use cases (high concision summaries, ticket routing, and automated response drafts). Per our ask, I pulled together a recommended shortlist of model candidates and a quick rationale for each covering cost, latency, and expected quality tradeoffs. Attached is a one-page benchmark summary and the prompt set we used.

Shortlist (recommended order):
1) Redwood-13B-q4 (recommended) — Best balance of latency and accuracy for your median 300-token tickets; good few-shot generalization; low cost with q4 quantization. Expected 99th pct latency: ~180ms/token on m60; unit cost: mid.
2) Open-13B-pt (high-quality variant) — Higher quality on long-form summaries, slightly higher latency ~220ms/token; useful for expanded summaries and sensitive language extraction. Unit cost: higher.
3) Llama2-70B-8k (fallback for complex queries) — Strong on reasoning/long context; significant cost and latency, use for sampled escalations only with explicit routing.

Notes / considerations:
- Benchmarks assume prefix KV caching for repeat tickets; we saw ~1.7x token cost reduction for your workload shape.
- Prompt set attached (acme_prompt_set_v1.csv) is the exact evaluation set we used — includes tickets across channels and tricky classification cases.
- We highlighted a handful of quality regression concerns (see page 2 of the PDF) where model outputs can drift on policy-sensitive extraction; recommend adding those prompts to CI/eval.

Next steps I recommend:
- Rishi to share the full benchmark numbers and the Drive folder with perf traces (by EOD tomorrow).
- If acceptable, schedule a technical deep-dive next week to validate end-to-end latency with your staging traffic (30–45m).
- I'll prepare a pricing/commit sketch for Dedicated capacity and a DocuSign quote for review.

Attachments: acme_benchmark_summary.pdf (1 page), acme_prompt_set_v1.csv (sample prompts)

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Hi Alex —

Putting the numbers here and uploading the trace artifacts to Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3Cacme-benchmarks.

Redwood-13B-q4 (on m60 / NVLink fabric):
- median per-token latency (512-token total request): 165ms/token
- 95th pct per-token latency: 255ms/token
- Inference throughput (batched): ~220 tokens/s (with continuous batching enabled)
- Cost estimate (hosted, on-demand): ~$0.012/token equivalent (depends on batching and KV cache hit rate).

Open-13B-pt:
- median: 200ms/token; 95th pct: 320ms/token; throughput ~180 tokens/s; cost ~25–30% higher than Redwood-13B-q4.

Llama2-70B-8k (fallback):
- median: 420ms/token; 95th pct: 700ms/token. Heavy variance depending on seq length.

Notes:
- Numbers above assume warm instances with KV cache warmup. For cold start we saw initial latency increases (~1.3x) until KV warms.
- We instrumented the prompt_set_v1.csv outputs and included a small sample of model responses in the Drive folder for the hallucination review. We flagged 12/200 prompts where the 13B models introduced minor factual hallucinations (mostly dates/IDs).
- Recommendation: Add the flagged prompts to your CI eval harness and configure a regression alert (we can enable this in Redwood Console).

I've attached the full benchmark PDF (acme_benchmark_summary.pdf) and the prompt exports to this thread. If you want, we can run a short A/B in your staging with a traffic shadow to measure real end-to-end numbers.

- Rishi
